title: Quasi-coherence of derived internal Hom on algebraic spaces
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use schemes [def-pc-scheme], algebraic spaces with their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space], module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Z)$ for the full subcategory with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Derived tensor is computed by K-flat resolutions and derived direct image by K-injective resolutions. A perfect complex is etale locally represented by a bounded complex of direct summands of finite free modules [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]. Let $S$ be a scheme, let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$, and let $K,L\in D(\mathcal O_X)$. Suppose either (i) $K$ is perfect and $L\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$, or (ii) $K$ is pseudo-coherent (etale locally represented by a bounded-above complex of finite free modules), $L\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$, and $L$ is locally bounded below (every point has an etale neighbourhood and an integer $c$ on which $\mathcal H^i(L)=0$ for $i<c$). Then $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(K,L)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] has quasi-coherent cohomology. The bounds in (ii) may vary with the neighbourhood. No Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0A8A, lemma-quasi-coherence-internal-hom, cases (1) and (2), applied etale locally for the locally bounded-below formulation.

proof.text: Choose a jointly surjective etale scheme covering $u_\alpha:U_\alpha\to X$. In case (ii) refine it by the neighbourhoods in the hypothesis, so $L_\alpha=L|_{U_\alpha}$ has a lower bound $c_\alpha$. Etale restriction is exact and preserves quasi-coherent cohomology by [lem-sfb-space-derived-etale-chart-calculus]; consequently each $L_\alpha$ is quasi-coherent and retains its chosen cohomological bound. Perfectness and the specified bounded-above finite-free models restrict to further slice covers by their definitions. Moreover $K$ has quasi-coherent cohomology: on each model its terms are finite free or direct summands of finite free modules, hence quasi-coherent; the summands are images of their splitting idempotents, and its cohomology is a cokernel of an image in a kernel. All these operations preserve quasi-coherence by [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-kernels-colimits]. The chart criterion then gives quasi-coherence of $K$ globally. No common bound over the cover is used.

source.place: Tag 0A8A, lemma-quasi-coherence-internal-hom, reduction to schemes; Tag 08F2, lemma-check-quasi-coherence-on-covering; spaces-properties.tex Tag 03M1, lemma-properties-quasi-coherent.

proof.text: Fix one of these scheme charts $U=U_\alpha$. Apply [lem-sfb-derived-etale-zariski-equivalence] to obtain $K_0,L_0\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{U,\mathrm{Zar}})$ and isomorphisms $\epsilon_U^*K_0\cong K|_U$, $\epsilon_U^*L_0\cong L|_U$. In case (ii), $H^j(\epsilon_U^*L_0)=\epsilon_U^*H^j(L_0)=0$ for $j<c_\alpha$. Exactness and faithfulness of $\epsilon_U^*$ imply $H^j(L_0)=0$ for these degrees (a faithful functor reflects a zero identity). In case (i), [lem-sfb-etale-detects-perfect] makes $K_0$ perfect. In case (ii), [lem-sfb-etale-pseudocoherence-descent] makes $K_0$ pseudo-coherent. Indeed a bounded-above finite-free representative is $m$-pseudo-coherent for every $m$: truncate it stupidly in degrees at least $m$ to obtain a bounded finite-free complex mapping to it, with the same cohomology above $m$ and a surjection in degree $m$. Thus the descent criterion applies in its stated sense.

source.place: Tags 071Q and 08H8, lemma-derived-quasi-coherent-small-etale-site and lemma-epsilon-flat; Tags 08HE and 08HG, lemma-descend-pseudo-coherent and lemma-descend-perfect.

proof.text: On the Zariski ringed site of $U$, put $M_0=R\mathcal Hom(K_0,L_0)$. In case (i), [lem-sc-rhom-supported-qcoherent-perfect-part] applies because $K_0$ is perfect and $L_0$ has quasi-coherent cohomology, without any bound on $L_0$. In case (ii), [lem-sc-rhom-supported-qcoherent-pseudo-part] applies because $K_0$ is pseudo-coherent and $L_0$ has the single lower bound $c_\alpha$ on this chart. In both cases $M_0$ has quasi-coherent cohomology. We use no support or uniform global boundedness conclusion.

In case (i) we compare only locally; no global comparison map is needed. Since $K_0$ is perfect [def-pc-perfect-complex], choose an open covering $U=\bigcup W$ with $K_0|_W\cong P$ in $D(\mathcal O_W)$ for a bounded strictly perfect complex $P$, and represent $L_0|_W$ by any complex $N$. The small etale site of an open $W$ is the slice $U_{\mathrm{et}}/W$, and $\epsilon_U^*$ followed by restriction to it is $\epsilon_W^*$ of the Zariski restriction (the pullback comparison of [lem-sfb-derived-etale-zariski-equivalence] for the open immersion $W\to U$). By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] on both sites, $M_0|_W\cong R\mathcal Hom(P,N)$ and $R\mathcal Hom(K|_U,L|_U)|_W\cong R\mathcal Hom(\epsilon_W^*P,\epsilon_W^*N)$. By [lem-sfb-ringed-site-strict-perfect-hom], ordinary $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,N)$ and $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(\epsilon_W^*P,\epsilon_W^*N)$ compute these derived Homs, even for unbounded $N$. For a finite free term, $\epsilon_W^*\mathcal Hom(\mathcal O^r,N^j)\to\mathcal Hom((\mathcal O_{\mathrm{et}})^r,\epsilon_W^*N^j)$, $h\mapsto\epsilon_W^*h$, is the identity of $(\epsilon_W^*N^j)^r$; for a split summand it is its restriction to the split idempotent. Finitely many source degrees occur, so pullback commutes with the sums, and the identifications commute with $d_Nf-(-1)^nf d_P$. As $\epsilon_W^*$ is exact [lem-sfb-derived-etale-zariski-equivalence], $R\mathcal Hom(K|_U,L|_U)|_W\cong(\epsilon_U^*M_0)|_W$.

source.place: Tag 08JP, lemma-descend-RHom, case (2), finite strictly perfect calculation; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 08JH, lemma-Rhom-strictly-perfect.

proof.text: The object $\epsilon_U^*M_0$ has quasi-coherent cohomology by step 3 and [lem-sfb-derived-etale-zariski-equivalence]. In case (i), step 4 shows that the restrictions of $R\mathcal Hom(K|_U,L|_U)$ to the members $W$ of a jointly surjective etale scheme covering of $U$ have quasi-coherent cohomology, hence so does $R\mathcal Hom(K|_U,L|_U)$ by [lem-sfb-space-derived-etale-chart-calculus]. In case (ii), [lem-sfb-zariski-etale-pseudocoherent-rhom] directly supplies $\epsilon_U^*M_0\cong R\mathcal Hom(\epsilon_U^*K_0,\epsilon_U^*L_0)$: its hypotheses are pseudo-coherence of $K_0$ and the lower bound $c_\alpha$ for $L_0$, already verified in step 2. With the chosen isomorphisms of step 2 this identifies $R\mathcal Hom(K|_U,L|_U)$ with $\epsilon_U^*M_0$. In both cases $R\mathcal Hom(K|_U,L|_U)$ has quasi-coherent cohomology.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] to the object $U_\alpha$ of $X_{\mathrm{et}}$: $R\mathcal Hom_X(K,L)|_{U_\alpha}\cong R\mathcal Hom_{U_\alpha}(K|_{U_\alpha},L|_{U_\alpha})$. Each right hand side is quasi-coherent by step 5. The jointly surjective etale scheme-cover criterion of [lem-sfb-space-derived-etale-chart-calculus] now implies that $R\mathcal Hom_X(K,L)$ has quasi-coherent cohomology. The proof used each $c_\alpha$ separately, so it also covers varying local lower bounds and imposes no Noetherian, separation, or quasi-compactness assumption.
